mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns due to reduced discount rates for equity valuations, with the signal active at all times without additional regime conditions.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When both housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceed their respective 3-month moving averages, it indicates strengthening consumer demand and economic activity, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns as corporate earnings prospects improve.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both above 3-month MA
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS are above their 3-month moving averages, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.5% year-over-year), rising inflation pressures trigger central bank tightening, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns as real rates rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL indicates high inflation (YoY > 3.5%), the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) consistently signals robust economic output and corporate capacity utilization, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns as earnings growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO is rising (month-over-month > 0.5%), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) exceeding 2.0% annualized signals strong economic expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns as corporate earnings and consumer spending accelerate.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized in the last quarter
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) and declining unemployment (UNRATE) occur simultaneously, it indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS is rising and UNRATE is falling, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, strong housing starts (HOUST) above 1200 thousand units signal potential overbuilding and impending economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns as investors price in a downturn.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST > 1200, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
